known_limitations: cargo-fuzz defaults to the musl target, where ASAN is incompatible with a statically linked libc (error: sanitizer is incompatible with statically linked libc). All X3 fuzz builds must pass --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.
cargo-fuzz requires nightly for -Zsanitizer; the repo default toolchain is stable 1.90.0. The fuzz gate must select nightly explicitly.
pkg-config is absent on this host; openssl-sys must be pointed at the system OpenSSL via OPENSSL_LIB_DIR/OPENSSL_INCLUDE_DIR or its build fails.
Only 2 of 98 fuzz targets have been exercised (compile_and_run, x3bc_engines). The pallet fuzz crates have not been built.
cargo-fuzz resolves its project as the nearest ancestor containing a Cargo.toml and then expects fuzz/ beside it; a validation fixture needs a parent manifest or cargo-fuzz walks to the repo root.
libFuzzer's value profiling solves memcmp against a constant, so a short defect trigger is found even from benign seeds; a stable negative control must bound the input space below the trigger length.

detection_validation.why: An installed tool is not an integrated tool (prompt §69/§90). This proves libFuzzer distinguishes a known-good fixture from a deliberately-broken one.
